hundreds of people had gathered outside the home of a businessman and stormed in to collect free clothing when the gates were opened.

As a Bengali, I kinda understand what happened.

During this time every year, everyone who were well off would collect extra clothes and donate them to the poor. Since everyone does it, the poor expect a yearly free-stuff day. They would swarm all over our cars, knocking on our windows for stuff. When we gave it to them, they often would fight over who gets it. I've seen an old lady punch a little kid for a bag of clothes.

Sometimes I definitely get pissed off but then realize these people don't have any other option. Bangladesh is a poor country and there really aren't any welfare programs. I think our donations were some of the few happy moments these people would get.

And thats not all. I've seen multiple people missing several limbs. I've heard that there are groups that would chop them off so that they could beg. They would have some crutches or roll by in a cart and come beg at you for stuff. Other times some beggars would say they're desperate for money. When my parents offered work for cash, they looked at us in disgust and demanded we just give them cash.

The life of a beggar in a third world nation is harsh.
